simple.meaning: מוֹרָשׁ (môwrâsh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a possession ; figuratively, delight.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 17:11. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מוֹרָשׁ (H4180) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מוֹרָשׁ (môwrâsh) / H4180 is traced through Job 17:11, Isaiah 14:23, Obadiah 1:17 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: “I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,” says Yahweh of Armies.
But in Mount Zion, there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will possess their possessions.

definitions.full: H4180. morash [ מוֺרָשׁ ] noun [masculine] a possession ; — construct קִמֹּד מוֺרַשׁ Isa 14:23 a possession for bitterns ; מוֺרָשֵׁיהֶם אֵת יַעֲקֹב בֵּית וְיָרְשׁוּ Obadiah 17 and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions (but read perhaps מורישׁיהם their dispossessors , ᵑ7 ᵑ9 ᵐ5 and others); figurative לְבָבִי מוֺרָשֵׁי Job 17:11 , i.e. my cherished thoughts (|| זִמּוֺתַי ), but figurative is questionable, see Di, who derives from ארשׁ desire, so Buhl.
